documents.title: FOR THE NIGHT MAN
lines: Whoever they sent —
Rounds are simple. Laundry, lights, leaks. Log it at the desk.
Demolition is on the 28th. Until then the company wants a body
in the building overnight. Insurance thing. You're the body.
Three rules, free of charge:
1. If you hear tenants, you don't. They're all gone since March.
2. The cameras record over themselves every six hours. Let them.
3. Don't photograph anything you wouldn't want developed.
I lasted four months. The pay is fine. The building is fine.
Everything here is fine as long as you don't look at it too long.

documents.title: NOTICE OF DEMOLITION
lines: HALCYON REDEVELOPMENT CORP.
PERMIT NO. 88-1141-C
The structure at 3 Ferrier Lane ("Halcyon Court", constr. 1961)
is scheduled for controlled demolition.
All units vacated as of March 30.
Utilities remain connected for site security purposes only.
Night security to be maintained until demolition date
per structural assessment file S3-61 (SEALED).
Questions regarding file S3-61 should not be directed
to this office.

documents.title: RETURNED MAIL — 2A
lines: (a letter, stamped RETURN TO SENDER three times)
Dear Mr. Ferrier,
I am writing again because your office does not answer the phone.
The management may consider me a nuisance. I consider myself
a tenant of forty years who has started appearing in other
people's photographs.
Mrs. Ilyes on 3 showed me her grandson's birthday pictures.
I am in the back of four of them. I was not at the party.
The man in the pictures holds his arms the way I do.
He is not me. He is CLOSE.
You will say it is my eyes. My eyes are fine.
It is the building that looks wrong on purpose.
— E. Kovan, Apt 2A

documents.title: UNSENT REPLY — 2A
lines: (dozens of drafts of the same letter; this one is the cleanest)
Eva,
You asked why I keep every newspaper. I will tell you and
you will laugh. Paper holds a day still. A day that is held
still cannot be re-arranged behind your back.
The building re-arranges. Slowly. Politely. Only the parts
nobody is holding still.
So I hold as much of it as I can.
Do not check on the dancer in 2C. She covers her mirrors
and she is right to.

documents.title: TAPED TO THE DRESSER — 2C
lines: House rules (mine):
— Cover the tall one at night. Not because of what you see.
Because of how long you'd look.
— A reflection is a room you cannot enter. Remember that
it works both ways.
— If your reflection is a half-beat late, LEAVE. Do not
check twice. Checking twice is how it learns the timing.
The company man said the mirrors came with the building.
All of them. 1961. Nobody makes mirrors for a building
before they know the tenants.
I dance with my eyes closed now. I recommend it.

documents.title: FRAMED PHOTOGRAPH
lines: A photograph of you, hanging in an apartment you have
never lived in.
No — look again. It's the caretaker's uniform, the standard
issue jacket. Anyone would look like that in this light.
The frame is warm.

documents.title: DEVELOPMENT LOG — J. MARSH
lines: Roll 44 — hallway, 3rd floor. Frame 12: a figure at the end.
Underexposed. Could be a coat rack. There is no coat rack.
Roll 45 — same hallway, bracketed. Frames 3-9: nothing.
Frame 10: the figure, one metre closer. SHARPER.
Roll 46 — I did not take roll 46.
It is not that the camera sees what I can't.
It is that the film gives it somewhere to stand still.
Every print is a rehearsal space.
I develop, therefore it becomes.
Stopped developing. Kept shooting. God help me I can't
stop shooting.

documents.title: FRESH PRINT — STILL WET
lines: A photograph of a man asleep in the caretaker's flat, 1B.
Taken from inside the room. From the foot of the bed.
You have never slept in 1B.
The exposure date stamp reads tonight.

documents.title: CRAYON ON PAPER — 3B
lines: A child's drawing of the building. Six windows are filled
with yellow crayon. One window is filled with grey.
In the grey window there is a tall thin figure, drawn with
more care than anything else on the page. The proportions
are wrong — arms too long, head too smooth.
Under it, in an adult's handwriting:
"He says it's the man who lives in the walls when nobody
watches. He says he only comes out where people look."
The drawing is dated before the building was finished.

documents.title: INCIDENT REPORT — MARCH 1961
lines: HALCYON CONSTRUCTION GROUP — FOUNDATION WORKS
During excavation for the southern footing, crew broke through
into a natural(?) cavity at a depth of 9m. Cavity extends
beyond lamplight in every direction tested.
Foreman Aldous lowered a lamp on a line. Line came back 4m
shorter than it went down. Line was not cut. Line was FOLDED.
Worker T. Brekke volunteered to survey the cavity and did so
for approximately 40 minutes. Upon return, Brekke was unable
to describe what he had seen, except that 'it was more there
the longer I looked.'
Brekke did not report for work thereafter.
Recommend: backfill and reroute footing.
Overruled by owner. See memo B.

documents.title: MEMO B — APRIL 1961
lines: FROM THE OFFICE OF A. FERRIER
Gentlemen,
The cavity will be capped, not filled. A service level will
be poured above it. Designate the cavity SITE 3 in all
further correspondence. There will be no further correspondence.
As to the incident: the surveyors' instruments disagree with
each other and with themselves. Measurements taken twice do
not repeat. Photographs of the cavity develop with detail
that was not observed at exposure.
I am advised these are instrument errors.
I am advised by other parties that attention is a nutrient.
I have decided to believe the first advice and bill the second.
Cap it. Build on it. Rent every unit with a view of something
else.
— A.F.
(taped behind the last page: a small brass key stamped S3)

documents.title: COMPLAINT LEDGER 1963—1988
lines: 1963 — 2 complaints — 'man on the stair who is not there twice'
1967 — 4 complaints — figure in lobby mirror / figure on lawn
1971 — 4 complaints — 'my television shows the hallway'
1975 — 9 complaints — footsteps above the top floor
1979 — 11 complaints — 'the man is clearer now' (3 households,
same phrasing, tenants unacquainted)
1983 — 19 complaints — withdrawn. All nineteen. Same week.
1987 — 31 complaints — ledger entry in unknown hand:
'HE IS ALMOST DONE'
1988 — ledger discontinued by order of management.
(marginal note, pencil: 'we stopped counting, not them')

documents.title: NIGHT WATCH LOG — OCT 1987
lines: Mon — Quiet. Cameras fine. New monitor hums.
Tue — Figure on CAM 4, 03:10-03:14. Four minutes. Didn't move.
Went up. Hall empty. Rewound tape: figure gone from the
RECORDING TOO. Tape remembers what I do, not what it saw.
Wed — Did not watch the cameras. Best sleep in weeks.
Thu — Watched CAM 4 all shift. It stood where I could see it.
I think that's the point. I think it stands where it is
seen because being seen is what it eats.
Fri — It stood closer to the lens.
Sat — It stood closer.
Sun — I have requested a transfer. I recommend the company
hire a blind man. I am not joking. I have never been
more serious about a staffing suggestion in my life.

documents.title: WORK ORDER — 4A (UNRESOLVED)
lines: UNIT: 4A    DATE: 11/85    PRIORITY: (crossed out twice)
Tenant reports 'seeing himself' in the unit. Not a mirror
issue. Maintenance attended, found tenant seated on a chair
facing the north wall. Tenant stated he was 'keeping it
where he could see it.'
Tenant relocated by family in December.
Unit sealed by management order — not for structural reasons.
The order reads, in full: 'Nobody looks at 4A.'
ACTION TAKEN: none
ACTION POSSIBLE: none

documents.title: SCRATCHED INTO THE PLASTER
lines: The wall above the chair is scratched with the same words,
over and over, in handwriting that starts careful and ends
as furrows:
IT LEARNS BY LOOKING
IT LEARNS BY BEING LOOKED AT
THE DIFFERENCE STOPPED MATTERING IN OCTOBER
Lower, small, level, calm:
if you are reading this you are teaching it to read

documents.title: STICKY NOTE — 4C
lines: Moving-out checklist:
[x] bed by the window   <- IT WAS BY THE DOOR
[x] table in the middle <- IT WAS BY THE WINDOW
[ ] stop coming back to check
The furniture is where I left it. I am no longer sure
I am who left it.

documents.title: POSTED FLOOR PLAN
lines: HALCYON COURT — SERVICE LEVELS
B1: boiler, records, storage.
The plan shows nothing below B1.
The stairwell you just used continues below B1.
Someone has drawn an arrow pointing down past the edge
of the paper. The arrow is drawn in crayon.

documents.title: SITE 3 — SURVEY FRAGMENT
lines: (stencilled on board, half the figures water-damaged)
SPAN, EAST: 44.2m / second reading 39.7m / third reading
'declined to repeat'
DEPTH: [illegible] 'depth is a courtesy here'
ECHO TEST: returned 6 seconds late. Returned TWICE.
NOTE (Chief Surveyor): The chamber grows more precise
under instrumentation. Rock face smooths where sighted
repeatedly. It is being finished BY the measuring.
RECOMMENDATION: no photographs. No drawings. No further
descriptions in writing, including this one, which I am
advised to end immediat

documents.title: EQUIPMENT TAG — 1961
lines: PROPERTY OF HALCYON CONSTRUCTION — SURVEY DIV.
A wooden tripod, decades old. No camera.
The mounting plate is worn bright, as if the camera was
attached and removed thousands of times.
Around the tripod's feet the concrete floor is polished
smooth in a perfect circle, the way stone is worn by
standing water.
Or by standing.

documents.title: PHOTOGRAPH, 1961 — REVERSE SIDE
lines: Handwritten on the back, in pencil:
'Footing crew, south pit. Third print of this negative.
The first two showed one man more than were present.
Each print he is nearer the ladder.'
'We have stopped printing it.'
You turn the photograph back over and count the workers.
You count them again.
The counts do not agree.

documents.title: LOOSE PAGE — NO DUST ON IT
lines: I came down to see it before they bury it under the rubble.
It isn't a monster. It never was. It is a description
that wants to be complete.
Sixty years of glances, photographs, complaint letters,
security tapes, rumours, nightmares — sixty years of us
drawing it from reference.
It has our posture now. It has a voice. It has almost
got a face. It is one long look away from done, and the
building comes down on the 28th.
It doesn't want to stop existing. Neither do I. That is
the only thing we have in common —
(the handwriting changes here, mid-sentence, into yours)
— that, and everything else.
